diagnosis: HBV calibrated on 1971-10 to 1997-12 using daily NSE, with DDS followed by a Nelder-Mead polish. Calibration NSE is 0.817, KGE 0.81, r 0.91 and PBIAS about +8%, so the model overpredicts volume. A split-sample test calibrated on 1971-1984 and run on 1985-1997 gave NSE 0.845. Two independent DDS runs converged to similar parameters: FC about 150-185 mm, BETA about 1, LP 0.55-0.7, K1 0.3-0.5, K2 0.08-0.14, UZL about 10 mm, MAXBAS about 2.5-3 days, and SFCF about 0.77 (this acts as a precipitation correction). I am therefore fairly confident the parameters will transfer to 1998-2008, and I expect NSE around 0.80-0.85. Weaknesses: the largest flood peaks are clearly underpredicted (simulated maximum about 32 mm/d against an observed 51-58 mm/d). Volume is overestimated by about 8%, which may come from reservoir regulation or abstraction and the urban area, which the model does not represent. Low-flow recessions are only approximated, given impermeable bedrock with some fractured and intergranular aquifers. Snow is unimportant (1.6% of precipitation falls as snow), so the snow parameters are poorly identified. CFR and CWH ended close to zero, but this has little effect.
